To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
triple-layered micromatrices can be used to achieve zero-order drug release profiles.

the design of a triple-layered micromatrix system comprising PLGA, PLLA and EVA can provide a tunable drug release profile, and this is achieved by controlling the layer thicknesses and by the diffusion of PGA oligomers from PLGA to PLLA.
we have designed multilayered microparticles for controlled drug release.
In summary, our research is concerned with
designing multilayered microparticles with tailored drug release profiles for the treatment of osteoporosis.
the fabrication of novel multilayered microparticles for the controlled release of drugs, which may have potential for the treatment of diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis.
the development of novel, multilayered, polymeric microparticle systems for tunable and controlled drug release.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the design of triple-layered PLGA/PLLA/EVA microparticle systems can provide a versatile and effective means of tailoring the drug release profiles to achieve a desired release profile for a particular application.
the use of triple-layered PLGA/PLLA/EVA microparticulate systems is a viable approach for the development of controlled release drug delivery systems.
this study has shown that the design of triple-layered particulate systems can provide a means to tailor drug release profiles, which may be useful in a number of applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design and fabrication of multilayered microparticles provides an attractive platform for controlled and tunable drug delivery systems.

we can design multilayered microparticles to achieve tunable drug release, and that this tunability is achieved through control of the layer thicknesses, the degradation properties of the layers and the migration of acidic oligomers from the outer layer to the inner layer.
triple-layered PLGA/PLLA/EVA microparticle system is a promising candidate for the design of a drug delivery system for sustained drug release applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the release profile of a drug from a microparticle can be tailored by controlling the layer thicknesses, the type of polymer used, and the drug localization within the particle.
the design of multilayered microparticles is a powerful tool for the controlled release of drugs.
the design of triple-layered particulate systems is a viable strategy to achieve tunable drug release kinetics.
